extra.message: Plaintext password storage/comparison in change_password endpoint — Passwords stored in plaintext DB are fully exposed on any DB compromise or SQL injection, and plaintext comparison offers no timing-attack resistance [verified: Line 26 compares current_user.password == current_password directly and line 34-36 stores new_password unhashed via update(), confirming plaintext storage/comparison with no hashing anywhere in this flow.]

Stored XSS via unauthenticated message API — An unauthenticated attacker can inject a script into the `message`/`from_user` fields via the public API, which executes in the admin's browser when messages are reviewed, leading to admin session compromise. [verified: MessagesView.post (line 43) has no admin_required decorator unlike sibling methods, storing raw message/from_user, which are rendered with |safe in admin/message.html:29-30 with no sanitization — confirmed stored XSS reachable by anonymous attackers against admins.]

Plaintext password storage and comparison — Any database compromise, backup leak, or admin-panel access exposes all user passwords in cleartext, allowing full account takeover and credential-stuffing against other sites. [verified: User.password is a plain String column with no hashing (models/models.py:11), and login/change_password compare and store the raw plaintext value (login/views.py:17, account_area/views.py:26,34-36), confirming plaintext credential storage/comparison.]

Reflected XSS via unsafe_params name parameter — Attacker crafts a link with a script payload in ?name= that executes in the victim's browser session, enabling session/cookie theft or actions as the victim [verified: request.args.get('name') flows directly to render_template with |safe, disabling autoescaping on attacker-controlled reflected GET input with no sanitization.]

Hardcoded weak SECRET_KEY and DEBUG mode enabled — A known SECRET_KEY lets an attacker forge or tamper with signed session cookies to impersonate any user (including admin), and DEBUG=True exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger/stack traces which can lead to remote code execution if reachable. [verified: SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source and DEBUG=True is set unconditionally with no env gate, so a forgeable session-signing key and the Werkzeug debugger are both live in any deployment of this code.]

Missing CSRF protection on account state-changing endpoints — An attacker can host a malicious page that auto-submits a form to /account_area/change_password or /change_email while the victim is logged in, silently changing their password/email and hijacking the account. [verified: No CSRFProtect/WTF_CSRF or per-request token exists anywhere in the app; change_email has no secret-dependent check so a cross-site auto-submitting form can hijack the account via session cookie alone. change_password is partially mitigated by requiring current-password, lowering its individual risk but not eliminating the missing-CSRF-protection finding overall.]

Missing CSRF protection on account state-changing endpoints — Attacker-hosted page can force an authenticated victim's browser to submit a forged request changing their password/email or injecting feedback messages without consent [verified: change_password, change_email, and send_feedback are POST routes guarded only by @login_required with no CSRF token check in the code or imports, so a forged cross-site request from an authenticated victim's browser would succeed.]

Missing authentication on message creation API endpoint — Unauthenticated attacker can flood the message store and, combined with the stored XSS sink, target admins with malicious content without ever logging in. [verified: MessagesView.post lacks @admin_required present on every sibling method in the same class, confirming unauthenticated write access to the message store, which also enables the stored XSS in finding 0.]

Plaintext password disclosure via user API — Any user calling GET /api/v1/users/<own_id>, or an admin viewing any user, receives the plaintext password in the JSON response, which combined with widespread password reuse enables account takeover elsewhere. [verified: User.serialize includes the plaintext password with no redaction, and UsersView.index (admin-only) returns it for all users; UsersView.get as written returns the raw User object (not .serialize) so it would actually raise a JSON-serialization error rather than leak via that specific path, but the underlying plaintext-password-in-API-response flaw is real and reachable via index().]

Reflected/Stored XSS via unsafe_cookies name cookie — Script execution in victim browser via crafted cookie or form submission, enabling session hijacking [verified: Cookie/form 'name' value is reflected via |safe with no sanitization; while cookie-setting requires some attacker capability (subdomain/MITM/social engineering) or the form path is directly attacker-controlled, the form-submission vector alone is a straightforward reflected XSS.]

Open redirect via next parameter in xss_protection toggle — Attacker crafts a link to the trusted domain that redirects victims to an attacker-controlled phishing site, aiding credential theft or malware delivery [verified: The 'next' parameter is taken directly from request.args and passed unchecked to redirect() with no relative-path or same-origin validation.]

Flask app runs with DEBUG=True unconditionally — Exposes verbose stack traces and, if reachable, the Werkzeug debugger console which can lead to remote code execution [verified: config_app() sets DEBUG=True with no environment conditional, exposing verbose tracebacks and the interactive debugger if this app is ever run as deployed rather than purely local dev.]

Default weak admin credential — If the deployment script is run without overriding the default password, the admin account is protected only by the well-known credential admin/admin, giving an attacker full admin panel access (including all user data and plaintext passwords). [verified: add_admin() defaults password to the literal string 'admin' when invoked without an argument, creating a well-known admin/admin credential with full admin panel access. This is an operator-invocation risk (CLI default) rather than a network-reachable sink, so severity is capped at medium rather than critical/high.]
